authorization: The supplied release registers these two literature assumptions. Their presence is a formal trust boundary, not a proof of the cited results.
policy: Only the two declarations named below are accepted. The requested approximation theorem and its numerical bounds are not admissible axioms.

WeightedMatching.bc21_seed_multiset_sele.formulation: Finite-state common-random-tape reformulation of the calibrated multiset selector and its arbitrary-subset failure guarantee.
premises: The finite seed prefixes are negatively associated.
The ordinary age kernel has the specified stationary initial law.
The miss kernel is exactly the joint age and artificial failure transition.
Every block multiplicity 1 <= r < m satisfies the reference stop-loss inequality at every real threshold in [0,1].
WeightedMatching.bc21_seed_multiset_sele.conclusion: There is a single probability space and a measurable prefix-only multiset selector, supported in the current multiset, whose arbitrary-subset nonselection probability is bounded by the corresponding stationary miss-word mass.

correspondence.calibration: Lemma 9.12, proved using Theorem 8 and Lemmas 9.13-9.15.
correspondence.arbitrary_subset: Lemma 9.11 is explicitly stated for any subset of rounds, after conditioning on the selected vertex's desired block wins.
correspondence.word_mass: The right-hand product of failures is the miss-age word mass for the specified age and miss kernels. The generic product/miss-row identity is kernel checked in ArtificialMiss.lean.
correspondence.common_tape: The independent randomness in Figures 2 and 6 can be fixed before all multiset inputs. The resulting procedure is a function of the input prefix and that tape. This is a realization convention of the published online construction.

limits: This declaration is not a kernel-proved theorem.
The reformulation combines the cited construction with its finite-state Markov and common-tape presentation; it is not a verbatim statement of one printed lemma.
It assumes no matching objective, dual feasibility, competitive factor, or new numerical feasibility bound.
The project's numerical all-multiplicity certificate must be proved separately.

source.title: Foundations of Modern Probability
locations: Countable product construction of independent random variables

WeightedMatching.kallenberg_independent_.formulation: Finite-output categorical randomization on a fixed countable common tape.
premises: The output type is finite and nonempty.
Each requested categorical mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one.
WeightedMatching.kallenberg_independent_.conclusion: There is one probability space and a draw function indexed by deterministic law, time, and slot. Draws are measurable in the tape, and every finite joint law at distinct time/slot coordinates is the product of the prescribed categorical laws.

correspondence.randomization: Apply the kernel randomization lemma to categorical laws, using one uniform variable per time/slot.
correspondence.independence: A countable product of uniform laws supplies independent coordinates.
correspondence.integrals: The finite joint expectation formula is equality in distribution, and every real function of finitely many finite-valued coordinates is bounded and integrable.
correspondence.causality: The actual sampled-history prefix identity is proved in LiteratureSampling.lean and is not part of this assumption.

limits: This declaration is not kernel proved in this repository.
Alternative laws at the same time/slot reuse the same random coordinate; no independence between alternative inputs is asserted.
It gives no selector, matching, competitive ratio, or numerical feasibility guarantee.
